chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Mahmud, from his father, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when Yusuf (peace be upon him) was in the prison, he complained to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about eating the bread alone, and asked for a condiment to dip it with. And there was much dry bread with him. So He commanded him to take the bread, put it in a pot, and pour water and salt over it, so it became 'Murayya', and he would dip it with it (peace be upon him).

key_terms.إِجَّانَة: A pot or vessel for cooking
key_terms.إِدَام: Condiment or dip used with bread
key_terms.مُرِّيّ: A dish made by soaking bread in liquid (water, salt, etc.)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and method of preparing Murayya according to Prophet Yusuf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the origin of 'al-Murrayya' (a bread-based dip or stew), linking it to Prophet Yusuf’s (peace be upon him) practical adaptation to the austerity of his prison confinement. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on finding ease and gratitude within divine decree, even in hardship, by transforming simple sustenance into a palatable meal through divine instruction.
